observations: One upright jar with an oval opening and rounded lower contour is retained at each width.
The interior dark oval, interior vertical boundary, outer side bands, and glass wall preserve the source inner/outer conductor distinction; no liquid or hand is introduced.
One central rod reaches the inner conducting region, with one rounded terminal above the rim.
The upper discharge arm approaches that terminal; the lower arm ends in a separate rounded ball adjacent to the outer coating. They share one right-side junction and one handle.
The upper and lower contact clearances remain qualitative, not calibrated source measurements. No wire bridges the lower clearance.
No distinct spark marks are present in the source or previews. The lesson describes possible sparks during discharge; an apparatus illustration need not invent a spark event.
All three previews are nonblank, framed, and visually coherent; the intended projected overlaps are retained without unrelated overlap or clipping.
